title: Computational Research Opportunities at NSF
session_title: New Funding Opportunities at NSF and Program Officer Panel Discussion
abstract: This talk will showcase several cross-cutting funding opportunities in which CBET actively participates, with a special focus on computationally relevant solicitations. The talk on opportunities will include the Computational and Data-Enabled Science and Engineering (CDS&E) meta program (PD 24-8084), the Cyberinfrastructure for Sustained Scientific Innovation (CSSI) NSF 22-632, Designing Materials to Revolutionize and Engineer our Future (DMREF) NSF 25-508, and others. The talk will also cover key solicitation-specific criteria and highlight notable pitfalls to avoid in proposals.

title: NSF: MRI/Mid-Scale Research Infrastructure Opportunities
session_title: New Funding Opportunities at NSF and Program Officer Panel Discussion
abstract: This talk will cover the main goals, parts of the proposal and review criteria for the Major Research instrumentation Program (NSF 23-519) and Mid-scale Research Infrastructure solicitations (NSF 24-598 and NSF 23-570) of the National Science Foundation. These solicitations aim to build research capacity. MRI awards are up to $4 million and support the acquisition or development of a multi-user instrument. Awards made under Mid-Scale Research Infrastructure may include any combination of facilities, equipment, instrumentation, or computational hardware or software, and the necessary human capital in support of the same.
presenting_author: Catherine Walker | National Science Foundation, Alexandria, VA
authors: Catherine Walker | National Science Foundation, Alexandria, VA

topic: NSF Special Solicitations: Proposal Submission Considerations
title: NSF Special Solicitations: Proposal Submission Considerations
session_title: New Funding Opportunities at NSF and Program Officer Panel Discussion
abstract: I n addition to support for core programs, NSF issues several special solicitations that focus on themes of emergent and national interest. For example, NSF and the Engineering Directorate support advances in data sciences, resilient manufacturing, resource-efficient industrial technologies, synthetic and engineered biology, imaging and biosensing, and tissue engineering and biomanufacturing. These solicitations often span various NSF divisions or directorates, or even other federal agencies. Special solicitations in CBET include NSF and Center for the Advancement of Science in Space, Inc. (NSF-CASIS) (NSF 24-502 and NSF 24-522), Future Manufacturing (FM) (NSF 24-525), NSF-NIH collaboration on biomedical technologies (Biomedical Research Initiative for Next-Gen BioTechnologies - SynBio Control (BRING SynBio)) (NSF 24-603), and ECosystem for Leading Innovation in Plasma Science and Engineering (ECLIPSE) (PD 24-110Z). This session will focus on how to submit proposals in response to special NSF solicitations. CBET Program Directors will highlight some current solicitations of interest to researchers, the key differences compared to regular (unsolicited) proposals, addressing solicitation-specific review criteria, common pitfalls encountered, and other important considerations to prepare competitive proposals.
presenting_author: Vamsi Yadavalli | National Science Foundation, Alexandria, VA
authors: Vamsi Yadavalli | National Science Foundation, Alexandria, VA

topic: Early Career Faculty Opportunities and Effectively Communicating with NSF Program Officers and Program Officer Question & Answer Panel
title: Early Career Faculty Opportunities and Effectively Communicating with NSF Program Officers and Program Officer Question & Answer Panel
session_title: New Funding Opportunities at NSF and Program Officer Panel Discussion
abstract: Understanding how to effectively communicate with program directors before proposal submission and after notices of declination are important skills to develop. Program Directors are invested in receiving and funding projects that push science and engineering forward in important and impactful ways. As such, they can be a source of important information and guidance if you know the right questions to ask and the most effective way to present them. This talk will also cover early career opportunities at NSF including the Faculty Early Career Development Program (CAREER) NSF 22-586 and the Engineering Research Initiation (ERI) solicitation, NSF 24-590. After the talk, a Q&A panel will be held with attending NSF Program Officers.
presenting_author: Steven Peretti | National Science Foundation, Arlington, VA
authors: Steven Peretti | National Science Foundation, Arlington, VA
